account:
Today appears largely routine, with no confirmed emergency or damage. I attended the morning market walk, went home for the noon lunch appointment, and returned to the town hall for one o'clock accounts. Several townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and bread at the inn; I also saw the baker put bread in the market stall chest. These observations fit ordinary baking and deliveries, and I have no evidence of anything more unusual. Some conversations were too distant to understand, so I cannot say what they concerned.

The builder has been seeking a defined repair scope and agreed payment. He reports finding no confirmed damage at the bridge approaches, ferry landing, or warehouse district, and says the secretary has received no repair requests. He proposed a more detailed inspection for two emeralds, with repairs subject to a separate agreement. I authorized neither paid inspection nor repairs, and he has acknowledged that decision. His stated purpose appears to be arranging properly specified work, not responding to an established defect.

The accounts appointment revealed a recordkeeping gap: the secretary has the appointment book but no accounts ledger or verified treasury balance. I have now inspected the treasury chest and found two stacks of 64 emeralds, totaling 128. That verifies its current contents, not prior income or expenses; I have no evidence of missing money.

My three o'clock appointment is tea with a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank, but the book gives no name or house number. The secretary checked cottages without identifying the host, and I do not remember who it is. This is an unresolved appointment detail, not evidence of a hidden purpose. I still need to find the host and keep that appointment, then return for office hours at four-thirty.
